name: Elizabeth (Eliza) Hamilton
notable_stories: Migrated to Ohio following the death of Jose Pierre, providing the link for the missing Ohio branch of the family
sources: Further Research on the Family and Descendants of Joseph P. and Elizabeth (Hamilton) Adams, William W. Allen (February 2012)
Descendants of Jose Pierre Adams, compiled by William W. "Bill" Allen (2 April 2011 edition)
Family research emails, 2011–2013 (John and Barbara Adams with Irma Kulp Zacher, George F. Adams, Bill Allen and others)
notes: CORRECTION 2026-09-23: Birth changed from "abt 1791" to "abt 1785". The 1820 and 1830 censuses place her birth between 1780 and 1790 (Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012). Decision by Brendan Adams.
Per Dale Morrow's Hamilton research, several of her siblings moved to Darke County, Ohio in the very early 1800s. [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 7356]
The 1850 census shows her living with the Gills, alongside a Sam'l Peer [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 8691]
Had at least one daughter and one son [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9674]
Received 25 1/2 acres in the distribution of her father's estate [Bill Allen, Further Research, 2012, line 9224]
Bill Allen’s hypothesis: Bill thinks she probably remarried soon after Jose died; no record of a remarriage has been found. [Bill Allen, line 4019]
Sources disagree: The 1850 census age suggests she was born about 1783, in Virginia. [Bill Allen, line 7497]

The family (and Bill's Uncle Ralph) long believed Gavin Hamilton of Mauchline was Eliza's father and sent her to Harper's Ferry, but the dates showed he was too old. [Family research emails, email 42]
Research lead (Francis Hamilton): A Francis Hamilton married Sarah Lee in 1818; the license was signed by Jose Adams. [Family research emails, email 41]
Research lead (Francis Hamilton): Francis Hamilton, Eliza's brother, was a close friend of Jose Adams. [Family research emails, email 41]
Research lead (Gill): In 1850 a Gill family in Licking County, Ohio, had Elizabeth Adams (76) living with them; Bill thinks one of her daughters married into it. [Family research emails, email 08]
Research lead (Samuel Peer): Samuel Peer, aged 19, was in the Gill household with Elizabeth Adams in the 1850 census. [Family research emails, email 08]
Research lead (Francis Hamilton): Francis Hamilton married a woman named Eliza (surname unknown). [Family research emails, email 20]
Research lead (Francis Hamilton): Francis Hamilton and his sister Mary owned a foundry in Harpers Ferry. [Family research emails, email 20]
Research lead (Francis Hamilton): The family holds a copy of Francis Hamilton's will, which left a small sum to the young George Francis Adams. [Family research emails, email 20]

Unconfirmed: Ralph Allen said Eliza and Francis Hamilton were siblings, children of Gavin Hamilton; Bill Allen says Eliza was a daughter of Francis and Susan Hamilton. [Family research emails, email 41]
Unconfirmed: George thinks Eliza and Francis were probably grandchildren of Gavin Hamilton of Scotland, based on a line of Gavin Hamiltons in the Virginia archives. [Family research emails, email 41]
Unconfirmed: She was born about 1783 according to later censuses, and was born and raised in the Harper's Ferry and Jefferson County area of Virginia. [Family research emails, email 12]
Unconfirmed: Bill Allen suspects she is buried in Luray Cemetery, but no record has been found. [Family research emails, email 13]
Unconfirmed: Family tradition says she and Francis were children of Gavin Hamilton, friend of Robert Burns. [Family research emails, email 20]
Unconfirmed: She and her brother Francis immigrated to Harpers Ferry in the 1800s. [Family research emails, email 20]

Unconfirmed: George F. Adams thinks the Scottish Gavin Hamilton lived too early to be the father of Eliza and Francis; they may be his grandchildren, or children of a Gavin Hamilton already in America. [Family research emails, email 29]
Unconfirmed: The Elizabeth in the Allen family records comes from a Hamilton family with many records at the Family History Library. [Family research emails, email 29]
Unconfirmed: Searching Scottish records, John found several Elizabeths with a father named Gavin, but no Francis. [Family research emails, email 35]

Open question: Were Eliza and Francis Hamilton children of Gavin Hamilton (Ralph Allen), grandchildren of Gavin Hamilton of Scotland via a Virginia line (George), or children of Francis and Susan Hamilton (Bill Allen)? [Family research emails, email 41]
Open question: Are Jose Pierre Adams and Elizabeth buried in Luray Cemetery near Hebron, Licking County, Ohio? Find-A-Grave lists no Adams burials there [Family research emails, email 12, 13]

Open question: Is the Elizabeth Adams aged 76 in the 1850 Licking County, Ohio census (Gill household) Eliza Hamilton Adams? Age 76 implies birth abt 1774, but email 07 gives abt 1783. Is the Gill household that of Stephen Augusta Gill, husband of Harriet Josephine Adams? [Family research emails, email 07, 08]

Open question: Hamilton Gavins: there are many Gavins in the line; Bill guesses the Gavin in later documents is the elder Francis's son. Gavin of Mauchline was thought to be Eliza's father (Uncle Ralph's version), but he was too old. [Family research emails, email 07, 42]

Open question: Email 20 says Mary Hamilton married Jos. Adams and her brother Francis married an Eliza (?), but emails 29, 35 and 36 (and the tree) treat Eliza/Elizabeth Hamilton as Jose's wife. Which name is right? [Family research emails, email 20, 29, 35, 36]

Open question: Email 20 says Gavin Hamilton, Robert Burns's friend, was the father of Mary/Eliza and Francis. Email 29 (George) thinks that timeline is too long: they may be his grandchildren or children of an American Gavin. Emails 35 and 36 (John) found no Francis born to a Gavin in Scotland between 1710 and 1800 and no Gavin old enough to be grandfather. [Family research emails, email 20, 29, 35, 36]

Open question: Which Francis Hamilton wrote the will leaving money to the adolescent George Francis Adams (#1) (email 20)? He is called Eliza's brother and a foundry owner at Harpers Ferry. The tree's Francis Hamilton Jr. died in 1821 when George was about 5, and Francis Alexander Hamilton (d. 1830) is recorded as Gavin's son, not Eliza's brother. [Family research emails, email 20]
Open question: John could not confirm Gavin as the father of the Francis purported to be Elizabeth's father (the tree's Francis Hamilton, husband of Susan). [Family research emails, email 36]

Open question: a record from around 1817 lists Elizabeth's husband as Jesse P. George F. Adams (Jr.) is sure this is Jose P. Adams. Should Jesse be added as an alias? [Family research emails, email 35]
